summary: SSE resume: out-of-order chunk delivery (chunk-skew) after reconnect behind CDN/edge proxy
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports partial/duplicated tokens and pieces of the final choice arriving out of order when resuming an SSE stream after a short network disconnect. Symptoms are consistent with an 'event reorder' window introduced by an edge/CDN buffer that replays buffered fragments and then forwards resume fragments, causing the client to see token fragments non-monotonically.

Impact: Intermittent correctness regressions in user-facing chat flows. Customer notices truncated final sentences or duplicated phrase prefixes ~2-10% of streams that resume after a reconnect during busy periods. No token-level billing mismatch reported, but application-level UX is broken for multi-turn assistant responses.

Environment: Production (prod us-east) behind customer's CDN (FastFront) in front of Redwood API. Customer on Dedicated plan with reserved capacity. Affected model: rw-instruct-large-v1, typical seq length 768.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Start an SSE chat streaming session from web client to hosted API through customer CDN.
2) Generate a long assistant response (tokens > 400).
3) Induce a short network interruption (e.g., client toggles airplane mode for ~2s) causing client to reconnect and resume with Last-Event-ID.
4) Observe resumed stream: some mid-stream fragments appear duplicated or the expected terminal fragment arrives earlier/later than its preceding fragment (order skew).

Expected behavior: Resume should produce monotonic, de-duplicated token fragments, with final choice properly stitched and single terminal end event.

Actual behavior: A subset of resumed sessions show chunk-skew: fragments are delivered in a non-monotonic order (e.g., fragment N+2 before fragment N+1) leading to partial phrase duplication or truncated final sentences. Problem appears more frequently when CDN edge has buffering enabled and when requests hit a different upstream backend instance after resume.

Logs & artifacts provided: customer attached network capture (pcap), SSE event stream snippets with Last-Event-ID headers, and timeline showing upstream instance id change on resume. Also included a short screencast of client-side reassembly failure.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge/CDN buffering with replay semantics can interleave buffered fragments and newly emitted resume fragments, producing out-of-order arrival at the client.
Hypothesis 2: Resume path lacks sufficient sequence validation — server accepts a resume token but downstream path may deliver older buffered items after resume completes, no dedupe enforced.

Findings: Reproduction succeeded when using a proxy that buffers and then flushes data on new TCP connection. Observed event-id overlap and instance_id mismatches in traces. No evidence of model-level token duplication; duplication happens during transport reassembly.

Logs: server-side stream logs show resume accepted at offset 12456 and backend emitted fragments 12457..12540. Edge replayed fragments 12458..12460 after resume ack, causing client to see 12458 before 12457 in wall-clock order.
Risk: Customers behind aggressive CDNs or with non-TCP-preserving middleboxes may continue to see this until fix/mitigation applied.
Workarounds tested: websocket fallback with sticky session eliminates issue in tests; disabling CDN buffering/coalescing reduced but did not eliminate occurrences for the customer.

Next steps: implement server-side monotonic resume enforcement, add dedupe suppression for recently-seen event-ids, and publish best-practice guidance for customers using intermediate CDNs. Coordinate rollout with Dedicated infra changes.
Estimated ETA for PR -> canary -> prod: 2 weeks (if no regressions).
resolution: In progress - mitigation and customer workarounds provided. Server fix in progress (PR opened to enforce monotonic resume and suppress re-emitted event-ids). Customer workaround: enable websocket fallback with sticky upstream, or disable CDN request coalescing at edge. We will coordinate a canary rollout and then full deployment. Final resolution will include a follow-up runbook entry and a confluence page update.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-14: PR #1984 created to add resume-id monotonic checks and a short-lived dedupe cache keyed by (session_id,event_id).
Temporary mitigation: recommended customer to set FastFront header 'X-Edge-Buffering: off' and to prefer websocket for long streams.
Follow-up: Add monitoring metric for 'resume_out_of_order_rate' and alert at 0.5% per-customer to catch regressions.
Postmortem plan: if rate remains >0.5% after rollout, schedule extended incident review and consider stronger guarantees at API gateway layer.
